issue_context.title: RecreatingTerminatedPod/RecreatingFailedPod/SuccessfulDelete events leak
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

The event `RecreatingTerminatedPod` is emitted ~10 times simultaneously after evicting pods of a Statefulset.



### What did you expect to happen?

The event should only be emitted at most once.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create a 1.29 kind cluster:
```
kind create cluster --image kindest/node:v1.29
```
 (tested with `sha256:eaa1450915475849a73a9227b8f201df25e55e268e5d619312131292e324d570`)

- Deploy a statefulset:

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
          name: web
```

- Get the initial `RecreatingTerminatedPod` event count for that sts:
```
kubectl get events  --field-selector involvedObject.kind=StatefulSet,involvedObject.name=web,reason=RecreatingTerminatedPod -o json | jq '.items[].count'
```
(shoud return nothing)

- Taint the node:
```
kubectl taint nodes kind-control-plane foo=bar:NoExecute
```

- Get the event count now:
```
kubectl get events  --field-selector involvedObject.kind=StatefulSet,involvedObject.name=web,reason=RecreatingTerminatedPod -o json | jq '.items[].count'
```
(got: `10`, `11`,`9`...)


The deletion of the Pod fails which make the controller enqueue the sts again and ask for another deletion and so on until the Pod is really deleted from the store.


`fieldPath="" kind="StatefulSet" apiVersion="apps/v1" type="Normal" reason="SuccessfulDelete" message="delete Pod web-0 in StatefulSet web successful"` is confusing as well.

- The same problem occurs with the event `RecreatingFailedPod`, deploy the statefulet:

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          sleep 3;
          exit 1
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
          name: web
```

When the Pods start `CrashLoopBackOff`, delete them, then ~10 `RecreatingFailedPod` events will be emitted.

- A simple update to the statefulset's spec also triggers a bulk of RecreatingTerminatedPod events.

- the `SuccessfulDelete` event leaks as well.

review_comments: why do we remove this test? is no longer valid?

This test was not removed. There was a code duplication and it was also split into two flavors, please see
- RecreatesFailedPodWithDeleteFailure
- RecreatesSucceededPodWithDeleteFailure

I do not see a use case behind this event. It is here only for tracking of the terminal phases.

Without this event we will still get the following events:

```
default       5s          Normal    Killing                   pod/nginx-roll-2                Stopping container nginx
default       4s          Normal    SuccessfulCreate          statefulset/nginx-roll          create Pod nginx-roll-2 in StatefulSet nginx-roll successful
```
I suppose we could move the event generation into the `updatePod` handler if we want to be backwards compatible. Thoughts?
Move or change here to logging seems acceptable.

@soltysh @atiratree this seem an important change in behavior to backport, we regressed last time we did something similar in this controller https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121389 , is not safer to backport only the spam logs changes?
@aojea please take a look at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123809#discussion_r1516888929. This was also causing a spam, but in the KCM logs.

We should try not to create the pods until the old one has been removed from etcd. Otherwise the kcm logs are getting spammed with:
 
```
 stateful_set.go:430] error syncing StatefulSet default/nginx-roll, requeuing: object is being deleted: pods "nginx-roll-2" already exists, the server was not able to generate a unique name for the object
```
